answer: Two devices sharing a room hear the same unpredictable background noise at the same instant, so identity can rest on cross-correlating short ambient clips recorded simultaneously by a phone and a nearby trusted device. Random hums and a passing car line up only for co-located recorders, while a farm faking locations must synthesise matching noise for every pair. A floor of timber creaks differently from stone, a beacon of shared sound anchors the match, and the karst of a hollow room shapes the noise in a way no scripted pair can copy.
